newsitem.title: USA: Calif. agency arranges reinsurance, taps Chase.
newsitem.headline: Calif. agency arranges reinsurance, taps Chase.

text.p: Nearly $2 billion of reinsurance has been arranged to support the California Earthquake Authority and Chase Manhattan Corp has been tapped for a $1 billion line of credit, officials involved in the complex authority said on Thursday.

The California Earthquake Authority (CEA) has secured from $1.8 billion to $1.9 billion of reinsurance, a key financial component of the earthquake authority plan, said Jack Graham, executive vice president and director at E.W. Blanch Holdings Inc, the authority's reinsurance broker.
California Department of Insurance spokesman Richard Wiebe said state Insurance Commissioner Chuck Quackenbush would now travel to meet with reinsurers in Europe and Bermuda to "seal the deals."
In another key development, Chase Manhattan has been selected to arrange a $1 billion line of credit for the earthquake insurance authority, Wiebe said.
"Everything is on track," Wiebe said, adding that the California Earthquake Authority was expected to begin selling policies as planned on December 1.
Graham said reinsurance companies in Germany, Switzerland, England and France had agreed to provide a significant amount of the CEA's reinsurance capacity.
"The reinsurance marketplace is all lined up," Graham said. "It was a project which took hundreds and hundreds of hours to convince them to support the CEA."
In late September, California Gov. Pete Wilson signed legislation to create the $10.5 billion publicly-run agency, which will sell earthquake insurance to homeowners.
Reinsurance and the line of credit are critical financial components of the earthquake authority plan.
